name: Bat
where: Caves and dark barns at night, including the Elysian Pool cave.
note: A 3-star animal and one clean hit. The Buck Antler Trinket can save a slightly damaged 3-star pelt.

name: Chipmunk
where: Forests across the eastern states.

name: Frog
where: Swamps, ponds, and riverbanks, especially after dark.

name: Rat
where: Towns, barns, and dumps, mostly at night.

name: Snake
where: Roads, rocks, and riverbanks. A few species exist only on Guarma during that chapter.
note: Rattlesnakes, water snakes, and the other small snake species share small-game arrows. Guarma snakes stay on Guarma.

name: Squirrel
where: Forests and the edges of camp.

name: Toad
where: Swamps and wet ground, especially Bayou Nwa.

name: Blue Jay
where: Forests in the eastern states.

name: Booby
where: Guarma only, during that chapter.
note: Chapter-locked to Guarma.

name: Cardinal
where: Woods and river country in the south and east.

name: Carolina Parakeet
where: Rare flocks in Bayou Nwa and Scarlett Meadows.
note: They are nearly gone. Killing the flock can wipe the species out of your game. Study them if you want them to remain.

name: Chicken
where: Farms and ranches, including Emerald Ranch.
note: Domestic. People nearby will react if you shoot their stock.

name: Crow
where: Fields, roads, and anywhere something has died.

name: Duck
where: Rivers, ponds, and Flat Iron Lake.
note: Some older lists call ducks a varmint target. This guide follows the small-game-arrow grouping used by the long GameFAQs pelt table. If a duck's compendium disagrees, trust the compendium.

name: Gull
where: Coasts and large lakes, including Flat Iron Lake and the southern shores.

name: Loon
where: Northern lakes and quiet rivers.

name: Oriole
where: Southern and eastern woods.

name: Parrot
where: Guarma only, during that chapter.
note: Chapter-locked to Guarma.

name: Pheasant
where: Meadows and field edges in the Heartlands and Scarlett Meadows.

name: Pigeon
where: Towns and farms.

name: Quail
where: Grassland and field edges.

name: Raven
where: Northern forests and mountain roads.

name: Robin
where: Forests and orchards.

name: Rooster
where: Farms and ranches.
note: Domestic.

name: Songbird
where: Woods across the map.

name: Sparrow
where: Towns, farms, and open woods.

name: Cedar Waxwing
where: Forests and berry bushes.

name: Woodpecker
where: Woods with standing dead trees.

name: Condor
where: Cliffs and desert sky in New Austin.
note: New Austin is epilogue country in a normal playthrough.

name: Cormorant
where: Coasts, Flat Iron Lake, and large rivers.

name: Crane
where: Marshes and shallow lakes. Whooping and sandhill cranes share this weapon.

name: Eagle
where: Cliffs and high country.

name: Egret
where: Bayou Nwa and Bluewater Marsh. Little, reddish, and snowy egrets share this weapon.
note: The exotic-bird stranger missions want specific egret plumes. Check that list before you skin them only for the satchel.

name: Goose
where: Lakes and wide rivers.

name: Hawk
where: Open country and tree lines.

name: Heron
where: Marshes and slow rivers.

name: Owl
where: Woods at night.

name: Pelican
where: Flat Iron Lake and the southern coast.

name: Roseate Spoonbill
where: Bayou Nwa.
note: Also wanted for the exotic-bird stranger requests.

name: Turkey
where: Woods and field edges. Wild turkeys, not the farm roosters.

name: Vulture
where: Desert sky in New Austin, and anywhere a carcass is drawing birds.

name: Armadillo
where: Desert scrub in New Austin.
note: Epilogue access in a normal playthrough.

name: Badger
where: Burrows in grassland and light woods, often at dusk.

name: Beaver
where: Beaver dams on rivers, including the Kamassa and Owanjila.
note: Ordinary beavers take the varmint rifle. The legendary beaver is a separate hunt and its pelt is not graded. One published grouping called beavers a repeater animal; the species notes and the GameFAQs table agree on the varmint rifle.

name: Gila Monster
where: Rocks and scrub in New Austin.
note: Epilogue access in a normal playthrough.

name: Iguana
where: Islands in Flat Iron Lake, and Guarma during that chapter.

name: Muskrat
where: Marsh banks and slow creeks.

name: Opossum
where: Woods and farms at night.

name: Rabbit
where: Meadows and the edges of camp.

name: Raccoon
where: Creeks and farms at night.

name: Skunk
where: Woods and fields at dusk.

name: Coyote
where: Plains and desert edges.
ammo: A regular arrow, or repeater rounds, to the head

name: Fox
where: Woods and meadow edges.
ammo: A regular arrow, or repeater rounds, to the head

name: Pig
where: Farms, including the Aberdeen pig farm and Valentine's stockyards.
ammo: A regular arrow, or repeater rounds
note: Domestic.

name: Alligator (small)
where: Bayou Nwa and the Kamassa shallows. Smaller than the bulls.
ammo: A poison arrow, or a rifle round to the head
note: Bull alligators are the large class and need an improved arrow or a scoped rifle.

name: Bighorn Ram
where: Rocky ridges in Ambarino, and again in New Austin during the epilogue.
ammo: A poison arrow, or a rifle round to the head

name: Wild Boar
where: Marsh edges and deep woods.
ammo: A poison arrow, or a rifle round to the head

name: Whitetail Buck
where: Forests. The buck is the antlered male.
ammo: A poison arrow, or a rifle round to the head

name: Whitetail Deer
where: Forests and meadows. Does and young deer use the same weapon as bucks.
ammo: A poison arrow, or a rifle round to the head

name: Cougar
where: Roanoke nights, Big Valley, and New Austin. They ambush.
ammo: A poison arrow, or a rifle round to the head
note: A rifle is the safer practical choice even though a poison arrow is a legal perfect-kill tool.

name: Goat
where: Farms and rocky homesteads.
ammo: A poison arrow, or a rifle round to the head
note: Domestic.

name: Panther
where: South of Rhodes and the forest south of Braithwaite Manor, often at night.
ammo: A poison arrow, or a rifle round to the head
note: The legendary Giaguaro is a separate hunt and only starts after Master Hunter 1 through 9.

name: Collared Peccary
where: Desert brush in New Austin.
ammo: A poison arrow, or a rifle round to the head
note: Epilogue access in a normal playthrough.

name: Pronghorn
where: Open plains in the Heartlands, and New Austin in the epilogue.
ammo: A poison arrow, or a rifle round to the head

name: Sheep
where: Ranches, including Emerald Ranch and the farms around Strawberry.
ammo: A poison arrow, or a rifle round to the head
note: Domestic.

name: Turtle
where: Bayou banks and slow southern rivers.
ammo: A poison arrow, or a rifle round to the head

name: Wolf
where: Forests and mountain roads, usually in a pack.
ammo: A poison arrow, or a rifle round to the head

name: Alligator (bull)
where: Deeper swamp in Bayou Nwa. These are the large ones.
ammo: An improved arrow, or a scoped-rifle round to the head

name: Black Bear
where: Forests in Roanoke, Big Valley, and the Grizzlies.
ammo: An improved arrow, or a scoped-rifle round to the head

name: Grizzly Bear
where: The Grizzlies and tall western forest.
ammo: An improved arrow, or a scoped-rifle round to the head
note: The legendary Bharati grizzly is a separate hunt.

name: Bison
where: Heartlands herds, and the snow herds near Lake Isabella.
ammo: An improved arrow, or a scoped-rifle round to the head
note: The White Bison and the Tatanka are separate legendary hunts.

name: Bull
where: Ranches and cattle towns.
ammo: An improved arrow, or a scoped-rifle round to the head
note: Domestic.

name: Cow
where: Ranches.
ammo: An improved arrow, or a scoped-rifle round to the head
note: Domestic.

name: Elk
where: Cumberland Forest, Roanoke, and Big Valley.
ammo: An improved arrow, or a scoped-rifle round to the head

name: Moose
where: Lake Isabella, the Kamassa around Brandywine Drop, and Owanjila. Ordinary moose are uncommon.
ammo: An improved arrow, or a scoped-rifle round to the head
note: The legendary moose near Brandywine Drop is a separate hunt.

name: Ox
where: Farms and freight wagons.
ammo: An improved arrow, or a scoped-rifle round to the head
note: Domestic.

name: Bluegill
where: Flat Iron Lake and other still water.
note: Bait is sold at the Lagras bait shop after A Fisher of Men.

name: Rock Bass
where: Lakes, including Flat Iron Lake and Aurora Basin.

name: Redfin Pickerel
where: Rivers and creeks, including Stillwater Creek in the epilogue.

name: Perch
where: Lakes and calm rivers, including the Elysian Pool.

name: Bullhead Catfish
where: Muddy rivers, including the Dakota and the water around Sisika.

name: Chain Pickerel
where: The Dakota River and southern rivers.

name: Steelhead Trout
where: Cold rivers in Ambarino and northern New Hanover.

name: Smallmouth Bass
where: Rivers, including the Dakota, and Lake Owanjila.
note: Easier to find as the story goes on. Fishing with Javier in Chapter 2 can put you on bass water earlier.

name: Largemouth Bass
where: Southern lakes and, in the epilogue, the San Luis River.

name: Muskie
where: Van Horn and large lake water.

name: Lake Sturgeon
where: Large rivers and lakes. The legendary one is a separate catch.

name: Northern Pike
where: Northern rivers.
note: There is no player-caught legendary northern pike on Jeremy Gill's list of 13.

name: Sockeye Salmon
where: Lake Isabella.
note: The legendary sockeye uses the Special Lake Lure instead of the ordinary river lure.

name: Longnose Gar
where: Bayou Nwa.

name: Channel Catfish
where: Large southern rivers.
note: The legendary channel catfish is not a fish you land. See that entry.

name: Legendary Bluegill
where: South of Clemens Point, on the shore of Flat Iron Lake.
note: Start A Fisher of Fish with Jeremy Gill at Gill Landing, on the northeast shore of Flat Iron Lake. Buy the special lures in Lagras. Mail the fish to Gill from a post office and do not let it fall off the horse. You can also discover this one if you fish with Kieran in Chapter 3.

name: Legendary Bullhead Catfish
where: Creek deltas west of Sisika Penitentiary. Row across the Lannahechee.
note: IGN also calls this fish the Legendary Catfish. The special river lure is the one both of that page's matching lists agree on.

name: Legendary Chain Pickerel
where: The Dakota River hairpin between Flatneck Station and Horseshoe Overlook.

name: Legendary Longnose Gar
where: The swamp between Lakay and Lagras in Bayou Nwa.

name: Legendary Largemouth Bass
where: San Luis River, southeast of Lake Don Julio. Epilogue access.
note: IGN's lure table says Special Lake Lure. The same page's location blurb says Special River Lure. Try the Special Lake Lure first.

name: Legendary Muskie
where: By the lighthouse at the south end of Van Horn.

name: Legendary Perch
where: Elysian Pool, near the waterfall, southwest of Annesburg.

name: Legendary Redfin Pickerel
where: The largest pool of Stillwater Creek, between Thieves' Landing and MacFarlane's Ranch. Epilogue access.

name: Legendary Rock Bass
where: Aurora Basin, at the head of the Lower Montana River, west of Manzanita Post.

name: Legendary Sockeye Salmon
where: Lake Isabella, in the Grizzlies West.
note: Ordinary sockeye use a river lure. This one uses the Special Lake Lure.

name: Legendary Smallmouth Bass
where: Lake Owanjila, west of Strawberry.

name: Legendary Lake Sturgeon
where: Off the railroad bridge at the mouth of the Lannahechee River, between Saint Denis and Rhodes. A boat works if you do not want to stand on the bridge.
note: IGN's February 2026 page puts it on the Lannahechee. Older guides put a sturgeon on the Dakota near Valentine. Use Gill's map marker if the bridge is empty.

name: Legendary Steelhead Trout
where: The Kamassa basin north of Annesburg, upstream from Brandywine Drop.

name: Legendary Channel Catfish
where: You do not catch this fish. During A Fisher of Fish II, Jeremy Gill is pulled under near the San Luis River in Rio Bravo.
note: After you have mailed the 13 legendary fish, the follow-up mission starts. You get Gill's hat and the Special Spinner. Do not look for a bite.
